questions.q: What two alerts does Sentinel correlate into a single multi-stage incident in this case study?
options: A workbook alert and a hunting query result
A Defender for Office 365 phishing alert and a Sentinel impossible-travel analytics rule alert, both naming the same Account entity
Two unrelated alerts from two different user accounts
Two separate impossible-travel alerts from the same analytics rule running twice
questions.explain: Because both alerts name the same Account entity, Sentinel merges them into one incident rather than leaving them as two disconnected alerts.

questions.q: What triggers the playbook that disables the account at 9:32 AM?
options: A scheduled analytics rule running once per day
An automation rule whose condition matches the Account entity and high severity
The user resetting their own password
A manual click by the analyst after reviewing the full case
questions.explain: The automation rule's condition is what decides which playbook runs and when — here, matching on entity and severity, with no analyst action required.

questions.q: Why does the analyst run a hunting query scoped to the flagged foreign IP address?
options: To find the user's original password
To disable the account a second time
To confirm whether that IP address touched any other account, which decides if this stays a single-user incident
To check whether the analytics rule's schedule needs to change
questions.explain: The hunting query checks for broader compromise — confirming the incident's scope before it's closed, the same technique from Lesson 30.

questions.q: What closure classification does the analyst assign to this incident?
options: False Positive — benign activity
Duplicate of a prior incident
Undetermined — insufficient evidence
True Positive — credential phishing leading to account compromise
questions.explain: The timeline, the playbook's automated response, and the hunting query all confirmed real malicious activity, so the incident is closed as a True Positive with a specific classification.

questions.q: What does the closing note require before the disabled account can be re-enabled?
options: A password reset and MFA re-registration
Nothing further — the account can be re-enabled immediately
The user must delete their email account
A new analytics rule must be written first
questions.explain: The closing note specifies the remaining remediation step — password reset and MFA re-registration — before the account is safe to use again.
